name: Winkeladvokat
author: Roland Siegers (Schmidt Spiele, 1986); implementation AGP
description: Roland Siegers' 1986 Schmidt Spiele scoring game (also L'avocat du diable / Devil's Advocate; later reworked on hexes as Cabale). The 8x8 board is printed with concentric rings of points — 2 on the rim, then 4, 8 and 16 on the central four squares. Your Avocat makes a WINKELZUG: a rook move over empty squares, a 90-degree turn, then another rook move — and you must drop one of your 25 Article tokens on the square where it turned, banking that square's number. Instead of moving the Avocat you may capture: one of your Articles jumps an orthogonally adjacent enemy Article into the empty square beyond, draughts-style, chaining as far as you like. Avocats neither capture nor are captured. The moment a player cannot move their Avocat the game ends; each player scores the numbers under their Articles plus one point per Article captured, and an equal total is an honest draw.
